- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–5% downward bias in next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-adjusted correction.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model may misread trend; use sentiment momentum (last 3 values) to weight correction.
